items.title: Some people will hate Tuesday's federal budget but Jim Chalmers doesn't mind
items.description: For once, the budget won't be a dull one. Jim Chalmers's tax reforms will create a stir and some question whether they will close the generation gap, but the treasurer is projecting a relaxed figure.

items.title: Military parades and promises of peace ring hollower than ever
items.description: Displays of military strength and perpetual promises of peace do little to mask the reality that major powers aren't always able to control the wars they helped create.

items.title: How sky-high property prices are limiting young people's life choices
items.description: Australia's regional housing crisis is decades in the making, the head of a research institute says. So can the federal budget fix it?

items.title: 'Out of sight, out of mind' is the most dangerous response to 'ISIS brides'
items.description: The political energy spent on the "ISIS brides" has not been matched by serious attention to the deficiencies in Australia's counterterrorism architecture.

items.title: Depth of antisemitism exposed by anonymous witnesses before commission
items.description: Fear, concerns for safety and the impact on children dominated the first week of hearings of the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion.

items.title: One bride is wearing $170k of jewellery. The other's family is being driven into debt
items.description: Foreign Correspondent crosses India to see how marriage has become big business.

items.title: Voters in Farrer set to elect new MP after three months in spotlight
items.description: After three months of intense campaigning, voters in the NSW electorate say whoever wins today's poll must act on the promise to make noise in Canberra.

items.title: Coalition's EV strategy risks appearing out of touch
items.description: The climate war is being won quietly, with nearly three in four One Nation voters eager to buy an EV.

items.title: Australia is breaking its carbon bond, but there's a cost
items.description: As Australia weans itself away from coal, aging power stations across the country have been reduced to smoke and rubble. But for communities at the coalface, there are serious and dramatic consequences.

items.title: US expects Iranian response on proposal to end war within hours
items.description: Iran and the US exchanged fire after weeks of relative calm in the Middle East, with each side claiming the other initiated the violence.

items.title: The biofuel industry is ready to expand. Here's what it says is holding it back
items.description: Billions of dollars worth of investment will flow if the federal government mandates a percentage of biofuels be added to the nation's fuel supply, major investors say.

items.title: Down-to-earth Attenborough 'likes a glass of wine just like you and I'
items.description: His legendary environmental documentaries have captivated generations, but away from the screen, Sir David Attenborough is "warm, well-informed and delightful company", too.

items.title: UK PM 'not going to walk away' despite catastrophic local election defeats
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer's Labour party has lost hundreds of seats in the local government election in England and has admitted defeat in Wales - which was previously Labour heartland.

items.title: The loophole that means employers don't need to pay these workers super
items.description: Despite working full-time hours, some private domestic workers are going years without superannuation contributions. Now, industry stakeholders are calling for change.

items.title: How a case of 'microplastic brain worm' led to this author's debut novel
items.description: Ellena Savage's debut essay collection, Blueberries, was a surprise hit. In her new novel, The Ruiners, she takes on Charles Dickens and the illegal waste trade.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of a Hitchcock classic, a popular dog breed and Gotye vs Carly Rae
items.description: Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, and the other is wrong. But there's a catch.

items.title: The day Australia's 'legislative machinery' was set in motion
items.description: More than 12,000 people packed into Melbourne's Royal Exhibition Building to witness the "pomp and ceremony" of a "magnificent" occasion in the country's history.

items.title: Mother's Day gratitude from a former foster child
items.description: Jaharn grew up in foster care from two years of age. Now 19, he and his foster mum share their lessons of love.

items.title: Australians with motor neurone disease fear losing fast-tracked NDIS
items.description: Australians with MND who have rapidly changing needs fear they will lose a priority pathway to access the National Disability Insurance Scheme under Labor’s planned changes.

items.title: Ukraine and Russia agree to three-day ceasefire, Trump says
items.description: US President Donald Trump takes to social media to announce a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine from May 9 to 11.

items.title: 'Is she still alive?' Aung San Suu Kyi's son in anguish
items.description: Aung San Suu Kyi's son demands proof his mother is still alive, as Myanmar's military junta keeps tens of thousands of political prisoners behind bars.

items.title: Farrer by-election candidates walk immigration policy tightrope
items.description: Many Farrer industries rely heavily on migration, while some communities face housing supply issues, making immigration a challenging topic for candidates.

items.title: Deaf and blind cricketers angered by changes to Cricket Australia's funding
items.description: Significant changes to how Cricket Australia funds Deaf, blind and intellectually disabled teams prompt concern from players and advocates.

items.title: De Minaur's disastrous clay court form continues
items.description: Struggling Alex de Minaur suffers another early clay-court tournament exit, this time at the Italian Open in Rome.

items.title: 'I don't coach for my job': Voss defiant after latest loss, Dogs edge Port
items.description: Carlton coach Michael Voss is frustrated after a close loss to Brisbane, but denies he is coaching for his job, while the Western Bulldogs hold off Port Adelaide despite being held to one goal in the second half.
